title: A Sublinear Time Algorithm for Opinion Optimization in Directed Social Networks via Edge Recommendation

problem.claim: Maximize the overall opinion in a directed social network under the leader-follower DeGroot model by adding k <= n edges from 1-leaders to followers.

contributions.claim: The objective function is monotone and submodular.
A deterministic greedy algorithm is proposed with approximation ratio 1 - 1/e and O(n3) running time.
A fast sampling algorithm based on l-truncated absorbing random walks and sample-materialization techniques is developed with sublinear time complexity O(kn1/2 log3/2 n/ε3) for ε > 0.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real networks are reported to evaluate the algorithms.
On undirected graphs, the fast sampling algorithm is reported to outperform the state-of-the-art method in efficiency and effectiveness.
On directed graphs, the fast sampling algorithm is reported to be as effective as the deterministic greedy algorithm, and both are reported to outperform baseline strategies.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies opinion maximization in a directed leader-follower DeGroot social network.
The objective is optimized by adding up to k new edges from 1-leaders to followers.
Monotonicity and submodularity support a deterministic greedy algorithm with a 1 - 1/e approximation ratio and O(n3) running time.
A sampling-based algorithm using truncated absorbing random walks and sample materialization achieves sublinear stated time complexity.
Experiments report comparative performance on undirected and directed real networks, including scalability to directed graphs with over 41 million nodes.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports a sublinear-time sampling algorithm with stated complexity O(kn1/2 log3/2 n/ε3).

interpretation.claim: Sampling and materialization may reduce computation for large-scale opinion optimization.

application.claim: Consider sampling-based approximations when exact or greedy optimization is too costly on large directed networks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the conditions under which the stated complexity or performance comparisons hold.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact network assumptions, algorithmic constants, or proof details.
The abstract does not provide experimental datasets, baselines, parameter settings, or quantitative results.
